stem: A hospital is reviewing sharps safety after a needlestick injury. Which OSHA requirement is most relevant when an effective, clinically appropriate safer device is available?

options.A: Continue conventional sharps when annual staff training is documented because engineering controls are optional if workers understand needlestick risks.
options.B: Allow each worker to decide whether to use a safety device because employer selection of engineering controls is not required for bloodborne-pathogen compliance.
options.C: Evaluate and implement an effective, clinically appropriate safer medical device, such as a needleless system or sharp with engineered injury protection.
options.D: Replace disposable sharps with reusable needles whenever possible because repeated sterilization is the preferred engineering control for needlestick prevention.

rationale: OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens standard requires engineering and work-practice controls to eliminate or minimize employee exposure. OSHA states that when an effective and clinically appropriate control such as a safety-engineered sharp exists, the employer must evaluate and implement it; the standard specifically includes needleless systems and sharps with engineered sharps-injury protections as engineering controls. C is therefore correct. Training does not replace engineering controls, the obligation is not left solely to individual workers, and reusable needles are not the preferred safer-device control.
educational_objective: Apply OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens requirements by using effective, clinically appropriate safer medical devices and engineering controls to reduce occupational sharps exposure.

source_original.stem: A hospital is reviewing sharps safety after a needlestick injury. Which OSHA requirement is most relevant when an effective, clinically appropriate safer device is available?

options.A: Continue conventional sharps when annual staff training is documented, because engineering controls are optional if workers understand needlestick risks.
options.B: Allow each worker to decide whether to use a safety device, because employer selection of engineering controls is not required for bloodborne-pathogen compliance.
options.C: Evaluate and implement an effective, clinically appropriate safer medical device, such as a needleless system or sharp with engineered injury protection in use.
options.D: Replace disposable sharps with reusable needles whenever possible, because repeated sterilization is the preferred engineering control for needlestick prevention.

source_original.rationale: OSHA requires employers to use engineering and work-practice controls to minimize bloodborne-pathogen exposure and to evaluate and implement effective, clinically appropriate safety-engineered sharps when available. Option C states that requirement. Option A incorrectly treats training as a substitute for engineering controls. Option B incorrectly shifts the employer's control-selection obligation entirely to individual workers. Option D substitutes reusable needles for the safer-device controls OSHA describes.
source_original.source_detail: OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens — Evaluating and Controlling Exposure: engineering and work-practice controls must minimize exposure; employers must evaluate and implement effective, clinically appropriate safer medical devices such as needleless systems and sharps with engineered sharps-injury protection when available. correction_summary: Retained construct and key; tightened option C by removing the awkward phrase 'in use' and verified the employer obligation directly against 29 CFR 1910.1030 and current OSHA guidance.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Needlestick prevention and OSHA engineering controls
audit_findings.source_authority: Federal OSHA regulation and official guidance.
audit_findings.currentness: 29 CFR 1910.1030 and OSHA guidance current in 2026; page includes June 2026 updates.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final wording reflects mandatory employer use/evaluation of effective safer controls without adding a device-specific mandate where clinically inappropriate.

distractor_audit.A: Training cannot replace required engineering/work-practice controls.
distractor_audit.B: Employer has an explicit evaluation/implementation obligation.
distractor_audit.D: Reusable needles are not identified as the preferred engineering control.

audit_findings.cueing: Parallel compliance choices; no second defensible answer.
audit_findings.blueprint: Workplace safety and safe equipment use.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Checked exact regulatory language and avoided universalizing one specific safer device to all clinical contexts.
